newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds up at short-end, weaker at long-end.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds up at short-end, weaker at long-end.

text.p: Irish bonds strengthened at the shorter-end of the curve but longer-dated government paper was weaker in active late trade on Thursday, dealers said.
Dealers said a close eye is likely to be kept on the currency markets after a bout of profit-taking had sparked a bruising overnight sell-off of sterling.
Sterling's latest tumble of nearly six pfennigs and four cents did not signal a fundamental change in the UK currency's attractiveness for yield-hungry investors, analysts said.

"People are continuing to buy Irish bonds at the short-end. We have seen some domestic interest but it has mostly come from overseas. We have seen good foreign interest in the five-year area for the last two weeks," one dealer said.
"Overall, the market continues to be positive," the dealer added.

By 1620 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had risen 15 pence from Wednesday's close at 103.10 to yield 5.65 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had slipped 25 pence from the close at 110.00 to yield 6.45 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 84 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area and 141 basis points over bunds in the five-year area.
